predicate_semantics: Truthiness test on an int field. self.states.overflowedResources is a StateValues dataclass field (KernelWriter.py:183), typed int and initialized to 0. The branch `if self.states.overflowedResources:` is taken iff the field holds a nonzero value. Within checkResources and upstream code it is assigned a resource-overflow CODE in {1..8} by 8 independent write-paths (see slice write_paths): code 1 = vgprPool.size() > regCaps[MaxVgpr]; code 2 = sgprPool.size() > regCaps[MaxSgpr] or allocTmpSgpr overflow listener; code 3 = half/bf16 single-element store; code 4 = numWorkGroupsPerExecUnit < 1; code 5 = ClusterLocalRead/oneBuffer scheduling conflict; code 6 = _ScheduleIterAlg==2 and CUOccupancy<2; code 7 = invalidLSUCode (empty LSU acc-VGPR range); code 8 = LdsNumBytes > archCaps[DeviceLDS]. The PREDICATE OPERATOR itself (int truthiness) is trivially solver-tractable; what DRIVES the field value is the aggregate of register-pool sizes and occupancy figures computed during full kernel generation plus rocisa per-ISA caps -- none expressible as a direct CLI/YAML input at this site.

z3_encoding.predicate_note: Python truthiness of an int n is (n != 0). The seeded domain is the int range [0,8] (representative values {0,1}); the SAT result is bounded to that integer range, hence solver_status=sat-bounded.

z3_model_output.validation: Both Z3 models re-evaluated through Python int truthiness bool(n): TRUE model bool(1)=True, FALSE model bool(0)=False (exact match). z3 4.16.0 run in-container tl-char, real model output.

true_examples.why: Field = 1 (code=1: vgprPool.size() > regCaps['MaxVgpr']). Nonzero -> truthy -> branch taken. Z3 model. Representative of any nonzero code 1..8.

Field = 8 (code=8: kernel['LdsNumBytes'] > archCaps['DeviceLDS']). Any nonzero overflow code makes the predicate True; this is the upper bound of the seeded domain. By-value witness (set by an upstream LDS-capacity write-path, not directly solvable at this site).

false_examples.why: Field = 0 (initial value; no overflow path fired: every register pool fits, occupancy OK, no LSU/LDS/scheduling/dtype overflow). Falsy -> branch NOT taken. Z3 model. Dominant runtime case for a valid solution.

    """Pure model of KernelWriterAssembly.py:1902 branch predicate.

    set to a resource-overflow code in {1..8} by any of 8 upstream write-paths.

crosshair.caveat: Absence of a counterexample is NOT a proof. CrossHair confirms the post-condition holds over the seeded precondition, cross-checking the Z3 SAT witnesses. The domain is finite (9 values) so the Z3 models are the load-bearing evidence; CrossHair corroborates the pure operator only -- it says nothing about which upstream write-path actually fires at runtime.

notes: CLASSIFICATION RATIONALE -- solver-backed-under-assumptions (NOT fully-static, NOT purely runtime-dependent). The branch PREDICATE is a bare int-truthiness test, which Z3 solves both ways over the seeded [0,8] domain (true_val=1, false_val=0, both sat, re-validated by Python bool()). The ASSUMPTION is that the field self.states.overflowedResources independently carries one of its possible values: in reality the value is produced by 8 distinct upstream write-paths whose conditions depend on vgprPool.size()/sgprPool.size() (register high-water marks accumulated across the entire kernel-generation pass), getOccupancy() output, numWorkGroupsPerExecUnit (rocisa PhysicalMaxVgprCU + getNextFreeVgpr high-water), invalidLSUCode (LSU scheduling), and rocisa per-ISA regCaps/archCaps/asmCaps tables. Those drivers are runtime/codegen-state, not direct CLI/YAML inputs at this site, so the witnesses for the field VALUE are by-value (code=8) / solver-modeled over the seeded int (codes 0,1). The predicate operator is decidable and witnessed; the precondition on the field's value is supplied as an assumption -> solver-backed-under-assumptions. No isinstance / nodeType dispatch / os / filesystem at the predicate operator; the rocisa caps are static per-ISA tables (not live GPU queries, per slice notes) but are still upstream codegen state rather than predicate inputs.
